case: Suprema, Inc. v. International Trade Commission
citation: 742 F.3d 1350 (Fed. Cir. 2013), vacated on reh'g en banc, 796 F.3d 1338 (Fed. Cir. 2015)
summary: Section 337 reaches articles whose direct infringement happens only after importation, when the importer induced it. The ITC finds a violation and issues exclusion and cease-and-desist orders; a Federal Circuit panel vacates the inducement ruling; the full court grants rehearing en banc and upholds the Commission, and the panel then affirms. Exercises the ITC pack end to end, the ITC -> CAFC link, and the state flags through a rehearing grant (panel-mixed set, cleared by rehearing, panel-affirmed set) down to cert-not-sought.

legs.context: Cross Match Technologies files a Section 337 complaint against Suprema (Korea) and Mentalix (Texas) over fingerprint scanners (Inv. No. 337-TA-720, Certain Biometric Scanning Devices).

steps.event: Respondents respond (the en banc opinion cites 'Suprema Answer'; route assumed)
Cross Match moves for summary determination on the economic prong of domestic industry
Summary determination granted only as to the economic prong (2011-03-18); the rest goes to hearing
Hearing concludes (the hearing itself is not confirmed in a primary source; route assumed)
Final initial determination: violation as to '993 claims 10, 12 and 15 and '344 claim 19; no violation as to the '562 patent
Recommended determination on remedy and bonding, issued with the ID
Cross Match, the respondents and the Commission investigative attorney each petition for review
The Commission decides whether to review
Review granted as to '344 claim 19 only (76 Fed. Reg. 52970)
The Commission reviews on the merits
Final determination: violation; Suprema induces Mentalix's direct infringement of '344 claim 19
Limited exclusion order, cease-and-desist order against Mentalix, 100% bond
The orders go to the President and USTR
No disapproval found in the sources read (route assumed)
Suprema and Mentalix appeal (Nos. 2012-1026, -1124, -1170, consolidated); Cross Match intervenes
Entries of appearance and certificates of interest
The Commission's and Cross Match's responses
Argued before Prost, O'Malley and Reyna, JJ. (date not found; route assumed)

'562 no-violation and '993 infringement affirmed; the '344 inducement ruling and the cease-and-desist order vacated; exclusion order vacated in part (O'Malley, J.; Reyna, J., concurring in part and dissenting in part)
The Commission and Cross Match weigh rehearing
The Commission and Cross Match petition for rehearing en banc
The full court considers the petitions
Rehearing en banc granted; the panel opinion is vacated
The appeal is reheard; the panel's mixed disposition no longer stands (argued en banc 2015-02-05)

En banc, 6-4 (2015-08-10): Chevron deference to the Commission's reading of 'articles that infringe'. On remand the original panel affirms the Commission on the '344 patent and reinstates its rulings on the others
No further rehearing petition found (route assumed)
Bill of costs (route assumed; the pack requires it)

outcome.real: The Commission's violation finding and exclusion order stand; no certiorari petition was found.

deadlines.trigger_event: the date the final ID issued (the 12 days actually run from service, which the sources don't date)
deadlines.arithmetic: 19 C.F.R. § 210.43(a)(1): 12 days, computed under 19 C.F.R. § 201.14(a) (via § 210.6(a)). The count begins with the first business day after the event: Friday Jun 17 -> Monday Jun 20 (day 1). Because the period is 7 days or more, calendar days are counted: day 12 = Friday Jul 1, not a holiday. Jun 20, 2011 was an ordinary business day; Juneteenth became a federal holiday only in 2021.
deadlines.historical: Petitions filed 2011-07-05, four days after this date. That suggests the ID was served after its issue date, or the time was extended; neither is in the sources read. (Before the engine's holiday calendar respected Juneteenth's 2021 start, the op anchored at Jun 21 and returned Jul 5.)

deadlines.arithmetic: Fed. Cir. R. 40(a)(1)(B): 45 days because the Commission, a U.S. agency, is a party (links.json patches cafc@itc). Dec 13 + 18 = Dec 31; + 27 = Jan 27 (45), a Monday.
deadlines.historical: Petition filing dates not found; rehearing en banc was granted in May 2014.

quirks: The en banc court decided only the statutory question and returned the appeal to the original panel, which affirmed on 2015-09-14. The CAFC pack has one fresh disposition after a rehearing grant, so the en banc decision and the panel's affirmance are one step.
The CAFC pack's panel-to-mixed has no remand branch; the 2013 panel also remanded the exclusion order for revision.
The ITC pack's own federal-circuit-review / cafc-remanded nodes duplicate the CAFC pack; with links on, the walk takes the link into cafc@itc.
